llm_evidence: ["‘Democracy means to me that we have the right to have our voices heard, whether it's through voting or free media. It's about fairness and equal rights for everyone, which is why I value courts so much – they're the backbone of upholding those principles.'", "Sure, like when cases involving minority rights are heard in court and judges make rulings that protect their rights, or when there's an issue with media censorship and the courts step in to ensure freedom of the press isn't violated. Those are the types of scenarios that make me feel strong about democracy and the role of courts in upholding it."]

["To me, democracy means that everyone's voice should be heard, and that laws are made through fair processes where people can argue their points and get their say in courts.", "Sure, courts help keep everyone accountable and make sure no one is above the law. Free media keeps things transparent and allows information to flow freely, so people can make informed decisions."]

["I think it's supposed to be about fair elections and having a say in how we're governed, but I've seen a lot of slow politics lately. It's like trying to fix a car with a Swiss army knife—sometimes just a hammer would do the trick quicker.", "Sometimes it feels like the politicians just can't seem to get things done. Like when there's a big problem that needs fixing, but the process takes so long that the issue just keeps piling up. It's like getting a project done on a spreadsheet instead of just hammering a hole through a fence."]

["I think democracy should be more efficient sometimes despite the need for back-and-forth.", "Involving a committee to streamline approvals and letting more people be involved earlier in the process is a good way to keep things moving and keep everyone's input."]
["It feels like my opinion doesn’t really matter as much.", "The people are supposed to have a say in how things are run, not just the politicians and judges."]

["To me, it's all about the will of the majority because that's who our leaders are supposed to represent, not those in power or the wealthy.", "They should aim to make decisions that help everyone, not just those with lots of money. It's like they're ignoring the majority."]

["Democracy to me is about everyone having a say in how things are run, kind of like when you and your friends decide what game to play.", "When it works well, democracy is when laws and decisions are made through fair voting, like when a class votes on a field trip."]

["sure, to me democracy means people have a say in how they're governed and the government acts based on what the people want. It's more than just voting every few years, it's participating.", "it made me feel like democracy works when the government helps out. They actually provided what people needed, which is important. Feeling supported helps people know their voices matter. That's when I really believe in how democracy should work."]

["To me, democracy means that everyone gets a fair shake, like equal rights and fair pay, and that public services are available for everyone. It’s about people having a say in how they’re governed and that those in power should also serve the public good.", "Public services should be funded through taxes that everyone pays, not just one group. And I think the communities or elected officials closest to where the services are used should largely decide how they are spent, like how many nurses there are at the hospital near where I live."]

["You believe better labor laws and increasing minimum wages would help both workers and businesses, suggesting a more balanced approach to democracy.", "I see wages being a big issue, and I think ensuring fair wages should be prioritized, even if it means higher costs for businesses at first."]

["Well, I've seen lots of changes in my lifetime, but I always valued stability and order. For me, democracy means keeping things as they are, where everyone knows where they stand, no need for too much debate or sudden shifts. That's how things run smoothly, in my book.", "We need those discussions to understand different ideas, but then we should move forward with practical steps. That's how democracy works best—finding solutions and then making them happen."]

["To me, democracy means keeping things steady and orderly, not too much debate or change. I think stability is very important for a society.", "Stability in society is like having a well-oiled machine. Everything runs smoothly, and there's less chaos and confusion. People know what to expect, and life is predictable and secure. That's important for people to feel comfortable and to make plans for the future."]
